text: Good evening. I call the November 11th, 2026 Legislative and Policy Committee meeting to order. Welcome everybody. I believe sign-up for public comment occurred before the meeting. I do not see anyone here for public comment, so we will move from item two of the agenda, item three, which is the draft minutes for the October 28th, 2026 meeting. Has everyone had an opportunity to review those meeting minutes? Any changes?

All right. I will entertain a motion to approve the meeting minutes. I'd like to make a motion as well to approve the meeting minutes. Thank you. Second. Thank you both. Mrs. Griffiths has made the motion to approve the meeting minutes from the October 28th, 2026 Legislative and Policy Committee meeting, with a second from Dr. Rashid. All in favor say aye. Aye. Aye. Aye. All opposed?

Hearing none, the motion passes three to zero with all school board members present voting yes. Now we will move forward to item four of our action items. This is 4.01 is Policy 2220, Clerk, and I will turn it over to Dr. Bergen. Thank you, Chair Svenson. By way of reminder, this policy was before you at your last meeting.

Policy 2220, Clerk, is up for its five-year review, having last been reviewed in November of 2021. The proposed changes before you align with current practice and provide additional clarity. The minor revisions are tracking the language of the code and standardizing the language across our policies. As is our custom, we put the policy out for feedback, and we did receive feedback from MSAC.

It's displayed on the screen. You also have a copy of it in your packets. It's available to the public, attached to the agenda item. The first bit of feedback occurs at lines nine and 10 in reference to others. The concern being raised by the feedback is others is not defined and could be anyone, and should that be defined, and should others be trained. I spoke with the clerk to ask who others might be that the clerk might normally

call upon, and typically the only other the clerk might call upon is the deputy clerk. So, if it's the will of the committee, staff is agnostic. We're okay with the word others. If you are not, we could substitute others with deputy clerk if you wanted to be responsive to that feedback. Would you like me to pause there before going on to the second? See if you want to entertain any motions with that. Sure. And Mr. Allen, I guess for

technical reasons, do we need to make a motion to be on the base motion for the purposes of the committee, or can we just vote to amend, vote on the amendment, and then move to the base motion? Thank you, Chair Svenson. I think either approach is fine for the committee level, but as long as the action taken reflects the amendments and you can vote on the base motion to close it out at the end. Great. Thank you.

All right, so I will make a motion to, in the redline version for Policy 2220 at line nine, replace the word others with the deputy clerk. Second. Thank you, Dr. Rashid. So I've made a motion to amend that language. Dr. Rashid has seconded. Any discussion on the motion?

All right. Hearing none, all members in favor of the motion say aye. Aye. Aye. All opposed? Hearing none, the motion passes three to zero with all school board members present voting yes. And we'll return to Dr. Bergen for further discussion on the policy. Second bit of feedback on this policy occurs at lines 11 and 12 in the use of the word may in the sentence, "The

clerk may maintain records in electronic format." Did speak with the clerk about this again. The recommendation was changed to shall. We do have some records that are in paper copy, particularly historical records. Many of the historical records have been archived into an electronic format, and just about everything we do currently would be in electronic format, but change the word to shall would not match our practice. So again, staff is agnostic.

We're okay with the word may, but I'll defer to the committee, and that concludes the feedback on this policy. Thank you, Dr. Bergen. I'm also comfortable with the word may here. Any further discussion? No. All right. I will entertain a motion to move this policy as amended to the full board as an information item. So moved. Second.

Thank you. Dr. Rashid has moved to forward Policy 2220 as amended to the full board as an information item. Mrs. Griffiths has seconded. Any further discussion? All right. All members in favor say aye. Aye. Aye. Aye. That passes three to zero, with all school board members present voting yes. And with that, we will move on to item 4.02, which is Policy 2430, School Board Agenda, and I will turn

it over to Dr. Bergen to present This policy was also reviewed at your last meeting for information. Policy 2430 was before the board last in August of 2023, so it's only been a couple of years. It's not a five-year change. The proposed changes are to bring the policy in alignment with changes in state law. State code updates require staff

to bring the policy to the committee to reflect these recent changes, which we reviewed with the committee in detail at your last meeting. We'd be happy to go back and address any questions that we weren't able to address in the last meeting relative to the changes. It went out for feedback. We did not receive any feedback from our advisories. However, there is one amendment posted by a member of the committee, so I will stop there. The administration has no more feedback to provide and turn it back

over to the chair. Thank you, Dr. Bergen. Members, any further discussion on this policy? Mrs. Griffiths. Thank you, Chair Svenson. I do have an amendment to this policy. Red lines five to six, "The agenda shall be published on the school division's official website prior to the meeting." As it's always been, the amendment should read, "The agenda and all supporting

materials shall be published on the school division's official website at least three days prior to all official school board meetings." That's my amendment. I don't know if you want me to speak to it further. Yes. Please do. The reasoning behind this is it's always been three days prior. I believe that if you don't have three days prior in there, we'll get documents for the board

and for the public to read at the very last minute, and they would be unprepared. I think putting at least three days in there should guarantee that the school board and the public get to see the information posted. Thank you. Thank you, Mrs. Griffiths. And is there a second for the motion? I will second the motion. So we are officially on that amendment. Board members, any further discussion on the amendment?

Yes, Dr. Rashid. Is this three business days, or is it a little bit specific than that? If I may ask, Mr. Allen, what was it before, three business days? Or actually, if I may, before you go ahead, when we get the information posted for our school board meetings, you post it Friday, and then it goes into the weekend, right? So I don't know if it's necessarily business days, correct?

Thank you, Mrs. Griffiths. It's my understanding from practice of the school board clerk, we'll post on the Friday before the Tuesday meeting, so that would be three calendar days as opposed to three business days. But I would recommend specificity should the committee approve Mrs. Griffiths' amendment. Dr. Rashid? Or yes, Dr. Rashid. I just wanted to verify.

I understand the policy's written as is, but what is the practice of LCPS, if you can refresh my memory? Is it three days that we recommend, just to reinforce that? Thank you, Dr. Rashid. So the current practice is that the proposed agenda is published on the school division's official website prior to the meeting, and that's required by 2.23707, so that's why we're

proposing this language on five and six. I will say for consideration, you may want to move that under Time Limitations, Section C, which starts on line 20. That seems like a more appropriate place for this provision. I did not catch that until reviewing the proposed amendment. But the current practice is the three calendar days

for the proposed agenda and supporting documents to be posted to BoardDocs before the full school board meeting. Three calendar days is what you're saying? That's correct. Okay. Thank you. No, thank you, Dr. Bergen. Yes, three. So Friday, Monday, Tuesday, three business days. That's correct. Sorry, I misspoke earlier.

And Mr. Allen, just to clarify where this practice comes from, because that three business days is not in this policy. So do you know the origin of that practice? Thank you, Chair Svenson. So there is a requirement for the notice of meetings to be posted three business days prior to a meeting. As the school board currently

has in practice, they, in every January at the annual organizational meeting, sets the schedule for the business meetings of the school board and posts that, and those get added to the school division's official website. So you're well in compliance with that requirement. So that's the requirement, that we have to have three days notice of the meeting itself, but there's no

legal requirement that we have to have it posted three business days, like the agenda and supporting materials posted three days before the meeting. That is correct. So what's required under the Virginia Freedom of Information Act is that at the same time that the school board members receive supporting documentation, the public receives supporting documentation, and that's achieved in the current practice through the posting onto BoardDocs. I see. And

as the existing policy states, board members receive agenda items, or are made aware of agenda items, at least two days prior to the meeting? That's at lines 22 to 23 of the red line version. Yes, Chair Svenson, that's the current practice of the school board pursuant to Policy 2430. All right. Thank you. And Dr. Rashid? One last question. For this detail

in lines five to six, including the amendment, is there any specificity regarding, or maybe I'm not reading the other sentences, if there's any way to tie it to being specific to either school board documents as the school board meeting or committee documents? Thank you, Dr. Rashid. I would make a recommendation to clarify. I think in Mrs. Griffiths' proposed amendment,

the phrase is "official school board meetings." I don't have it in front of me, school board meetings, but I think for clarity's sake, this committee may want to consider distinguishing between full school board meetings versus committee meetings. And with that, I don't know if Mrs. Griffiths would like to do a friendly amendment to that to be- Of course ... having specificity. Thank you. I would. Thank you very much.
And just for clarity of the record, what is the friendly amendment and change to the existing language in the amendment? Yes, that would be great.

So, the amendment I put forward was, "The agenda and all supporting materials shall be published on the school division's official website at least three days prior to all official school board meetings," but as a friendly amendment, we could add committee meetings as well, and have the proper verbiage for that, or advisement on the proper verbiage on how it should read. Yes, Dr. Rashid.

Thank you so much. And, Mr. Allen, you talked about general policy for school board meetings in terms of uploading documents and amendments. What is the policy or current practice, maybe not written down, for committee meetings? Thank you, Dr. Rashid. So currently, committee meetings would follow conceivably the 2430 convention, which doesn't specify this with as much prescription as Mrs. Griffiths'

proposed amendment does. I'm sorry, line 2430? No, Policy 2430. So it follows- Yeah ... the school board agenda. Okay, so you're saying that it's just the same as we do for regular school board meetings versus committee meetings? Correct, under the current iteration or version of this policy. So perhaps the friendly amendment would make Mrs. Griffiths' amendment read, "The agenda and all supporting

materials shall be published on the school division's website at least three days prior to all school board meetings," just deleting the word official, just because a committee meeting is a school board meeting. All of it. Doesn't have to be specific anymore. Okay. Yeah. Okay. So Mrs. Griffiths says that works. And then in terms of a

friendly amendment also, I know we had discussed specificity about business days versus calendar days, but would you accept the insertion of the word business days as well, Mrs. Griffiths? As far as the difference between business and calendar, I just want to clarify again, Mr. Allen, when we post on a Friday and it goes into the weekend, you're still considering Friday, because it goes late Friday night,

okay? You're still considering Friday, Monday, and Tuesday? Tuesday is partial because then we have the meeting. So, is there any way to clarify between the two, or it's pretty much the same? Thank you, Mrs. Griffiths. So it's my understanding, and this would be to administration and the board clerk and their interpretation, given that currently there is no such timeline here.

I guess two days is what this-- And so it's certainly within your purview as the committee to make the recommendation to the full board what you think would be an appropriate time. So currently, all I can say is because the business and calendar is kind of murky, but we know that Friday at 5:00 typically is when it's posted in advance of the Tuesday at 4:30 meeting. But the discretion of this committee is to make a recommendation to the full board.

And that would be calendar, going Friday, Monday, Tuesday. That would be calendar? Yes. That would be. It's not business because the business day usually ends at 5:00. Is that correct? That's the longstanding practice. Okay. I guess we would use calendar then. One

concern I have about the existing policy and potential changes here is that I think it's straightforward enough that agenda items are posted at least two days prior to the meeting under the current policy, and most supporting documents. But from time to time, there are supporting documents that new information has come in Or there has been last-minute changes, and that gets posted. And so I'm worried about constraining the ability to

update or edit supporting materials that are added to the agenda item itself. So I am curious to hear Dr. Bergen, Mr. Allen, your thoughts on that, and welcome feedback from my colleagues. Yeah. Administration would have the same concern. It's rare we

don't have supporting documents in place. The board and the public have it on the Friday before, from the time they receive it on Friday through Saturday, Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, up to the time of the board meeting. But there are occasions where there are changes because we receive questions or new information, and we update. So we then send out notice when we have replaced a document or added a document. Oftentimes, board members are giving us amendments as well.

So there are other supporting documents that are added to an agenda right up until the time the meeting begins. I think it's for clarity, and I'll defer to legal, the three days. Is there a legal requirement, Mr. Allen, for the topics? The notice of meeting and topics. Thank you, Dr. Bergen. So the new requirement under Virginia law,

that is being proposed for insertion on section H, starting at line 66, discusses that items added to the agenda after the meeting commences would not be actionable unless in some specified circumstances. And so yes, the idea is the agenda has to be locked in if you want an item to be acted on without

not falling within any of these prescribed exceptions prior to the meeting's commencement. And to clarify, that does not include supporting materials. Is that right, Mr. Allen? That is correct. So Chair Svenson, in terms to address your concern, the committee could consider an additional sentence that reads, "The school board will consider supporting materials added

before the meeting's commencement," or language to that effect to provide for that flexibility, that there could be supporting materials to include board members in the minutes that are posted just prior to the meeting. Could you restate the proposed language again, regarding the supporting materials?

Yes, Chair Svenson. I had indicated language to the effect of the school board will consider supporting materials posted prior to the commencement of the meeting. You could also add a notwithstanding or something as a connector. Well, I guess there are supporting materials, though, that are offered during the course of a meeting, for instance, like an amendment.

Yes, Mrs. Griffiths. Thank you, Chair Svenson. I think as we currently do it, it is three days before, and if there's any changes, we all get a notice that says something was changed to board docs. Today, I was just trying to clarify it in the policy just to make sure that it stays that way. What I don't want to see is, and this has happened,

presentations are missing from the actual agenda, and we've gotten them an hour prior to the meeting. I really did not know what was going to be in the presentation. So that's what I don't want to see. So when adding the three days, that was part of it. But of course, minor changes, let's say the presentation is uploaded and somebody needs to make a change to it,

or an update, I get that. But the bulk of the presentation was there, so we got to view it before changes might have been made. That is my concern, and that is why I brought up the three days for the first paragraph. Thank you. Yes, Dr. Rashid. Thank you. I was just curious if we make these three days, this amendment,

does that mean, and again, I'm just thinking out loud here, does that mean we can't make amendments on the dais last minute? Does that eliminate that, or should we add that in as an amendment to the amendment? I'm sorry, Dr. Rashid, can you restate your question? Let's say a board member just wants to make an amendment right then and there on the dais and says, "Oh, I'm just going to make an amendment. I just thought of it last minute," during the presentation of that action item.

Can they do that, or does this eliminate that, the three-day rule? Thank you for the clarification, Dr. Rashid. Yes, board members can still make amendments on the dais without posting them in advance. And oftentimes, board members might do so in hearing input from the community or in the dialogue with other board members, and so that's incidental, and under Robert's rules, that's appropriate. It's just the actual item

that would be non-actionable if you put on a separate topic that wasn't included on the agenda beforehand, unless it's an emergency or foreclosed. Okay. Thank you. I guess my concern, confusion is related-- Maybe it's the definition of the phrase supporting document. Is an amendment a supporting document, or is that some other set of documents we're referring to?

Thank you, Chair Svenson. An amendment isn't a supporting document. However, the practice of the school board to avoid any surprises, they've been posting amendments, but I think it's clear. And just to avoid any confusion, you could clarify that in this proposed language to just crystallize that amendments are not considered supporting documents. Sorry. Amendments that are posted as a courtesy prior

to the meeting do not constitute supporting documentation under this policy. And is there any other, I guess, a motion other than an amendment? I'm trying to think of different types of materials that might not be supporting documents that we would want to ensure are not inadvertently excluded by the policy.

Yes, Mrs. Griffiths. Thank you, Chair Svenson. Just to clarify again, when I put this amendment forward, I knew it wasn't about amendments that happen on the day of. It was more so presentations or something separate, as you mentioned, Mr. Allen, something separate that nobody knew about, and it was not posted three days before, but maybe

it was posted an hour prior to the meeting. This amendment does not have anything to do with anything that comes up on the dais in discussion or anything like that. So I just wanted to clarify that. But if we need to change the way it sounds so there's no confusion, I would be okay with that depending on how it sounds. Thank you. Thank you, Mrs. Griffiths. I appreciate that. Dr. Rashid. I was just going to ask Mrs. Griffiths if she would be willing to change the word,

maybe, of supporting materials to maybe something more specific. Or maybe we could write example, like supporting materials such as presentations, something to offer some sort of distinctive item that you are referring to. With regards to supporting materials, when the agenda is posted, the word supporting means to me all documents with an item on the agenda

are there. Which means that it would be if it's a presentation or if it's costs or estimates or anything like that, it should all be there at least three days prior. Because those are items that myself, other school board members, and the public would probably like to take a look at before in that three-day time.

So when I say supporting documents, that's what that means, and I would like to keep it, because they are supporting documents for the agenda. And I've spoken to this before, that it should be when the agenda is posted, we should have all the items there. This does not include discussions or anything like that. All the items should be listed there on the agenda. So if there's

an item there, I would like to see supporting information for that item. Thank you. Yes, Dr. Rashid. Thank you, Chair. My only concern is the open interpretation of supporting materials. I understand the intention completely. I understand it. And I like that how it has the word agenda on it. It's more of a subjective term, even though I know what supporting materials could mean.

But I'm just worried in the future, board members will say, "Well, I'm supporting this to come forward. This does not fall under supporting materials." And then it becomes this, I guess, this interpretive type of challenge. So that's why I was asking just for something more specific. But I appreciate that. I'm just going to interject here just for clarity. So if I heard correctly,

it's looking like the committee's will is to have these apply to all meetings of the school board. And just for clarity, any meeting of an advisory committee would then be subject and beholden to this because advisory committees are committees of the school board. Thank you for that clarification, Mr. Allen. Mrs. Griffiths. Thank you, Chair Svenson. I've had people come to

me from the public and ask me, "Where is the supporting documents for that item on the agenda? It's missing." If I may, as far as the verbiage per our discussion, Mr. Allen, to read, "The proposed agenda and all supporting materials shall be delivered to each board member at least three days prior to all meetings of the full school board. At the same time, those materials shall be published on the school division's official website." We were going to

change official, I think you had mentioned that, Mr. Svenson. "Notwithstanding foregoing, the school board will consider supporting materials posted prior to and including during a meeting of the school board." So that's per your thoughts, Mr. Allen. Thank you, Mrs. Griffiths. I think that encapsulates the discussions. I would say I didn't hear if you distinguished between calendar or business days.

And then the official, I think that had been taken out before official school board meetings, but official website, that can stay. I can read it again. I think for this purpose, Mrs. Griffiths can--

I think maybe for the record, we'll withdraw the motion, and then we'll have Mrs. Griffiths reintroduce it. One further item for consideration, Mrs. Griffiths, would for introducing in the terms of a friendly amendment to this. I think Mr. Allen had noted that

notwithstanding that the current red line has this new language at lines five to six, that it might be more appropriate to put this in the section C under time limitations, the lines 20 to 23. And it might make sense just to edit that language and add in what we're trying to add in here.

Yeah. So I think, Ms. Griffiths, are you withdrawing your prior amendment and then to tee up a new amendment, which-- Yeah. Thank you, Chair Svensen. I can. To be perfectly honest, I wouldn't mind still having it between five and six, if possible. Because we had,

on the red line, "The proposed agenda shall be published on the school division's official website prior to the meeting." So it was there. My first amendment, original amendment, was to add the three days. Now we're changing a lot of the language, but I would like to have something at five and six if possible, Chair Svensen. Understood. All right. So

maybe we'll reset with the new amendment that includes that new language. So if you withdraw your existing one and reintroduce the language, and we can get to a second on that one. Thank you, Chair Svensen. I'll withdraw that first one, and the revised language would be, "The proposed agenda and all supporting--" Wait, hold on. Do we have a second? Second. Dr. Rashid has seconded. And this language,

And I would like to point out that that's in the first paragraph. So I think having to go further into the policy, you might not see it. I think it would stand out in the first paragraph if we were able to implement this. Thank you. Thank you, Ms. Griffiths.

So I just wanted to confirm that you want the full in front of the school board. Well, notwithstanding and foregoing, the school board will consider supporting materials posted prior to and including during a meeting of the school board.

superintendent. And then it seems like we should still have that guidance, but the rest of that section might be duplicative if we move it up to the top of the policy. So I wonder, Mrs. Griffiths, if you'd

consider a friendly amendment to add on a sentence to your amendment at the end of your amendment that reads, "Agenda items and supporting documents should be submitted to the division superintendent at least seven days prior to the meeting." Seven. Seven days, which is what's currently in the policy.

Sure, that would be fine. Okay. And part of that friendly amendment would be deleting lines 20 to 23, the time limitations section, and renumbering sections accordingly. That is correct, Mr. Svensen. All right. Thank you. Dr. Rashid? I'm actually in support of the amendment. The only thing is- So you're saying eliminate the entire section of C just so that it stands out in the first paragraph? if both of you are not in favor of that, it will have to move, won't it? This is a friendly amendment process, but I agree. It's a mean amendment. It's not a mean amendment process. Chair Spencer, would it be an amendment to an amendment, or will she rescind and

This policy was up for information at your last meeting. It's due for its five-year review. It has been updated to add information regarding retention schedules, a

version would be at lines 48 and 49. It's really more of a comment than a recommendation from MSAC. There is another meeting of that select committee this week, and that is an important add to the current MOU. Just to wrap up this discussion, it was a comment from MSAC. It recommended that we review and discuss this.
